facts.fact: Thilak is a Resin House member, 41, a tapper before he was an odiyan and a member for twenty-two years; he brings Neela the master's tea (Chathu's ginger blend) and calls her 'Master' without irony.
facts.why: needed because the outline names Thilak, 41, as the one who calls her Master.

facts.fact: Neela writes the members' names on a plank from the carpentry shed in lamp-black: thirty-one real names, nine blanks. Twenty-two (a girl) asks whether her roll names her; Neela says she cannot give it yet because giving a name means reading the entry aloud.
facts.why: needed to show the names beat; applies F011/F012 and does not change the rules.

facts.fact: Sample intake-roll names glimpsed by Neela: Thulasi, daughter of a salt-boiler, Pazhayangadi; Kumaran called Kuttu, a ferryman's son.
facts.why: needed to make the intake rolls concrete.

facts.fact: Neela keeps the Kettamala spearmen's spare spears for the grove pairs; Devan leaves eight men (Bhaskaran among them) and rides out with six.
facts.why: needed to show who guards the House after Devan rides back for ch 19.

facts.fact: Neela has kept a torn slip, her own page-slip, on the master's desk.
facts.why: closing image; minor. Note that F253 has Chathu keeping the intake slip, so the reviser may cut this line.
